mechanism: Core's signmessage handler takes cs_wallet, calls EnsureWalletIsUnlocked(*pwallet) FIRST (refs/bitcoin/src/wallet/rpc/signmessage.cpp:42-44) and only afterwards runs DecodeDestination / IsValidDestination (:46-53) and the std::get_if<PKHash> check (:55-58). Ours reverses the order: the handler decodes the address at src/wallet/signmessage.lisp:48, raises -5 "Invalid address" at :50-53 and -3 "Address does not refer to key" at :55-58, and reaches wallet-ensure-unlocked only at :60, inside the with-wallet-lock that resolves the signing key.
consequence: Pure error-code ordering on a locked wallet. A caller that submits a malformed or non-P2PKH address to a locked wallet is told which argument is wrong (-5 or -3) where Core tells it the wallet is locked (-13), so a client that branches on -13 to prompt for a passphrase sees an argument error instead and a client that branches on -5 to reject user input sees it where Core would not. No state changes on either path and no signature is produced in either tree, so nothing is lost -- and the messages themselves match Core exactly once the wallet is unlocked. The finding's own unverified half is now verified: the ordering does diverge, and it diverges for both bad-address shapes, not only one.
evidence: Container /Users/sen/common-lisp/bl-ga11v-misc-s3d, warm image, probe-d.lisp: a born-encrypted regtest wallet (create-wallet :passphrase ...), left LOCKED as Core leaves it, addressed through the real RPC handler. Output: (:LOCKED T :HAS-ENCRYPTION-KEYS T) (:LOCKED-GARBAGE-ADDRESS (-5 "Invalid address")) (:LOCKED-BECH32-ADDRESS (-3 "Address does not refer to key")) (:LOCKED-OWNED-P2PKH (-13 "Error: Please enter the wallet passphrase with walletpassphrase first.")) (:UNLOCKED-GARBAGE-ADDRESS (-5 ...)) (:UNLOCKED-BECH32-ADDRESS (-3 ...)) (:UNLOCKED-OWNED-P2PKH-SIGNS (:SIGNATURE-LENGTH 88)). Core returns -13 for all three locked cases; we return -13 only for the third. The unlocked rows are the positive control: the address checks still fire and a real signature is produced, so the divergence is ordering and not a missing check. Ours: src/wallet/signmessage.lisp:31-66. Core: refs/bitcoin/src/wallet/rpc/signmessage.cpp:42-58.
fix_shape: Move the unlock demand to the top of the handler, matching Core's sequence: take the wallet lock once around the whole body, call wallet-ensure-unlocked before bl.crypto:decode-address, then run the -5 and -3 checks and the key resolution inside that same lock. Today the lock is taken only for the key lookup at signmessage.lisp:59-61, so the change is a widening of the existing with-wallet-lock rather than a new one; keep the error codes and message strings exactly as they are, since those already match. A regression test asserts -13 for a garbage address, a bech32 address and an owned P2PKH address against a locked wallet, and keeps the unlocked -5 / -3 cases as the positive control so the reordering cannot silently delete the address validation.
